summary: v08 as a single decision with a stated probability, for pool models without log-probabilities: the judgement session only (no verification); the case score is the submitted p_ischemic.

Aspect B (tools and evidence): v08p with the library tool annotator_reference (the candidate re-judged against a Smrdel & Jager-style annotator-like ST reference that follows slow trends, steps and lead orientation) added to the first-message dossier, with a two-directional reading guide in its description.

Aspect A (knowledge): v08p with card-backed reference knowledge on QRS changes during ST episodes (positional step vs ischemic gradual QRS change, K14/K15/K18/K19), on episode recurrence as neutral evidence (K42/K43/K13), and K28 replacing the uncarded COVADIS elevation entry, each with two-directional use guidance.

Aspect B (tools and evidence): a02 with the library tool annotator_reference (the candidate re-judged against a Smrdel & Jager-style annotator-like ST reference that follows slow trends, steps and lead orientation) added to the first-message dossier, with a two-directional reading guide in its description and a pointer in the Context guidance (K22).

Aspect A (knowledge): a03 with card-backed reference knowledge for separating heart-rate related from ischemic ST change (new card a04-1, Faganeli Pucer 2012: steeper ST/HR slopes in LTSTDB ischaemic episodes; K01/K02 heart-rate-before-ST timing; K10/K26 depth at high heart rate; K24/K25 upsloping depression) and a four-reading, two-directional heart-rate guide replacing the old heart-rate bullet.

Aspect C (reasoning procedure): v08p with judgement.md rewritten as a fixed seven-item checklist (A real local change, B time course, C shape, D ST at matched heart rate, E position, F conduction, G noise), each given a FOR/AGAINST/NEUTRAL verdict, a list of non-evidence (signal quality, lead count, recurrence, K43) kept out of the findings, and probability bands set from the verdicts.

Aspect B (tools and evidence): a02 with the library tool record_st_overview (how often the involved lead sits at the candidate's level outside all candidates, the extremum's percentile in the record, hourly median ST and heart rate, and a whole-record ST trend image) added to the first-message dossier, with a two-directional reading guide in its description and a pointer in the Context guidance.

Aspect B (tools and evidence): a06 with the library tool annotator_reference (the candidate re-judged against a Smrdel & Jager-style annotator-like ST reference that follows slow trends, steps and lead orientation, K22) added to the first-message dossier next to record_st_overview, with two-directional reading guides that say how the local-reference and whole-record views relate and that a rarely reached level is not by itself evidence for ischaemia.

Aspect B (tools and evidence): a04 with the library tool ecg_statements (ECGFounder statements for the reference window and the candidate: repolarization, injury-pattern, serial ST, conduction, axis and rhythm probabilities and their change from the patient's own reference) added to the first-message dossier as a second view independent of our fiducials and ST reference, with a two-directional reading guide in its description and a pointer in the Context guidance.

Aspect C (reasoning procedure): a08 with a heart-rate gate as judgement step 2 (the heart-rate change, the largest of rate_response's hr_rise_bpm, episode_dynamics' 5-min rise and episode rise over the 10-30 min baseline; heart_rate_related only allowed at 15 bpm or more, rate_response's surge minimum), the four heart-rate readings restricted to an open gate with the upsloping reading limited to depression, and two-directional closed-gate checks (normal-heart-rate shifts K29, no-rise ischemia K08, gradual build-up K16 versus step/position K14, drift via annotator_reference, early-repolarization elevation K32).

Aspect A (knowledge): a01 with card-backed reference knowledge on QRS changes during ST episodes (position as a synchronous ST/QRS step with sudden onset and little heart-rate change, K14/K15, versus gradual ischaemic QRS change in the lead with the largest ST deviation, K18/K19), on recurrence as neutral evidence (K42/K43/K13) and K28 replacing the uncarded COVADIS elevation entry, each with two-directional use guidance that also tells how to check an annotator_reference 'step' in morphology_steps.

Aspect B (tools and evidence): a01 with the library tool hr_rise_ledger (heart-rate baseline and rise, heart-rate peak to ST extremum timing, seconds of ST still deviated after heart rate is back at baseline, and the patient's comparable heart-rate rises with their ST change) added to the first-message dossier, with a two-directional, card-backed reading guide in its description (K01/K02/K03/K04/K07/K08) and a pointer in the Context heart-rate guidance.

Aspect C (reasoning procedure): a07 with an evidence-sorting step before submission (five questions answered once each: real change, separate change vs usual level, position/conduction, heart rate, shape/size; a finding that only rules out a non-ischemic cause goes for ischemia only when that cause was plausible and never against it, a missing ischemic sign such as a stable QRS is not evidence against ischemia (K18/K19 describe transient ST elevation only) and a missing non-ischemic sign is not evidence for it (K14), tools answering the same question count once, and p is set from the answers' strength, not the number of findings).

Aspect B (tools and evidence): a09 with a new dossier tool st_shape_change (per involved lead, the J-point, ST-point, T-wave and QRS-amplitude change at the extremum against the same lead before onset and at matched heart rate, the share of the ST-point change present at J and a pattern line), with a two-directional reading guide that maps it to the Long-Term ST Database shape terms (J depression with positive slope, parallel shift, T into ST versus horizontal flattening, down sloping, elevation; K24/K25/K26) and pointers in the Context shape and depth guidance.

Aspect B (tools and evidence): a05 with the library tool annotator_reference (the candidate re-judged against a Smrdel & Jager-style annotator-like ST reference that follows slow trends, steps and lead orientation, K22) added to the first-message dossier, with a two-directional reading guide in its description, a pointer in the Context guidance and its reading wired into checklist item A (real local change).

Aspect B (tools and evidence): a09 with the library tool record_st_overview (how often the involved lead sits at the candidate's level outside all candidates, the extremum's percentile in the record, hourly median ST and heart rate, and a whole-record ST trend image) added to the first-message dossier, so that each case is judged on a record-wide scale as well as locally, with a two-directional reading guide (a rarely reached level argues against drift and reference effects but is not by itself evidence for ischaemia; a level the lead often sits at or slowly drifts to argues for them), a paragraph on reading it together with annotator_reference, and a pointer in the Context guidance.
